title: Metabolomics Analysis of the Diatom Cheatoceros Tenuissimus Using NMR and GC–MS
author: Alothman, Emwas, et al.

steps.title: Set up cold extraction environment
steps.instruction: Keep all samples, cell pellets and all solvents (HPLC‑grade methanol, chloroform, water) on ice throughout the procedure; adjust solvent volumes experimentally to match the harvested cell biomass.

steps.title: Perform initial solvent addition and mixing
steps.instruction: Add 320 µL of 100 % HPLC‑grade methanol and 100 µL de‑ionized water to each dried cell pellet, vortex for 60 s, transfer the mixture to a 3 mL glass vial, add 160 µL HPLC‑grade chloroform, vortex for another 60 s, then shake the vial for 15 min at 4 °C with a shaking speed of 350 rpm (cell mixer).

steps.title: Add water and chloroform, centrifuge
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL de‑ionized water to the tube, vortex 60 s; add a further 160 µL chloroform, vortex 60 s; centrifuge the mixture for 15 min at 4 °C at 3700 rpm (or higher) while leaving the tube lid loosely closed to avoid breakage.

steps.title: Separate layers and dry extracts
steps.instruction: Using long tweezers, remove the tube from the centrifuge and place it on ice; prepare labeled 2 mL cryovials; with a glass Pasteur pipette carefully transfer the upper polar (aqueous) layer without disturbing the middle interphase, leaving a small top‑layer cushion; then gently collect the lower lipid layer; dry the lipid fraction (~1 mL) and half of the polar extract (~500 µL) overnight in a speed‑vacuum concentrator, store both at –80 °C; keep the remaining ~500 µL polar extract wet at –80 °C for later GC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Prepare NMR samples
steps.instruction: Thaw dried extracts at room temperature; for polar samples dissolve in 500 µL D₂O containing 0.05 % TSP; for non‑polar samples dissolve in 500 µL deuterated chloroform containing TMS; vortex each sample twice for at least 1 min per vortex; transfer the solutions into 5 mm NMR tubes.

steps.title: Acquire 1H NMR spectra
steps.instruction: Run each sample on a Bruker 800 MHz AVANCE NEO spectrometer equipped with a TCI cryoprobe (¹H/¹³C/¹⁵N); use the “zgesgp” pulse program and acquire ≥500 scans per sample; process data in TopSpin 4.2.0 (phase and baseline correction) and calibrate chemical shifts to 0.00 ppm using TSP for polar spectra and TMS for non‑polar spectra.

steps.title: Identify metabolites using Chenomx
steps.instruction: Open Chenomx NMR Suite 9.0, load the calibrated spectra, and fit each identified peak with a local baseline and Voigt functions to obtain metabolite assignments.

steps.title: Prepare GC‑MS samples and controls
steps.instruction: Transfer 100 µL from each wet polar extract into individual cryovials; prepare internal‑standard aliquots of an amino‑acid mixture at 1 µL, 2.5 µL, 5 µL, 10 µL, 25 µL and 50 µL; set up three empty cryovials as method controls; combine 100 µL from each of the four replicate extracts to make a pooled QC; dry all samples (including standards, controls and pool) for 30 min in a speed‑vacuum.

steps.title: Make derivatization solution
steps.instruction: Mix 10 µL of a hydrocarbon mixture (C7‑C40) with 1 mL BSTFA (N,O‑Bis(trimethylsilyl)trifluoroacetamide); shake the solution for 30 min at 37 °C and 1500 rpm in a multi‑thermal shaker.

steps.title: Derivatize samples and load GC vials
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of the derivatization solution to each dried sample, pooled QC, internal‑standard aliquot and method‑control tube; incubate for 1.5 h at 30 °C with shaking at 1500 rpm; afterwards transfer 30 µL of each derivatized mixture into a GC vial equipped with a deactivated insert for injection.

steps.title: Process GC‑MS data in Compound Discoverer
steps.instruction: Import the GC‑MS files into Compound Discoverer; impute missing values using the Random Forest (MissForest) algorithm; apply quality‑control correction as described in the referenced protocol; analyse batches of up to 15 files, normalising each sample to the maximum peak‑area mean of the batch.
